blocks.text: If a two-component mixture is a solution of a solid in water or another solvent, it can be separated by simple distillation. Sea water is not drinkable because it is a mixture of many soluble inorganic compounds in water; to remove them, sea water is distilled. Fractional distillation is another type of distillation, used to separate two liquids that are soluble or miscible in each other, for example a mixture of water and ethyl alcohol heated in a distillation flask.

blocks.prompt: What is the difference between simple and fractional distillation, and where is fractional distillation used in daily life (Quick Check 15.3)?
blocks.explanation: Simple distillation boils off a solvent from non-volatile dissolved solids and condenses it; fractional distillation uses a fractionating column to separate two miscible liquids whose boiling points differ by about 25 degrees C. Fractional distillation separates crude petroleum into petrol, diesel, kerosene and furnace oil, and ethanol from fermented liquor.

items: Simple distillation: solvent from a solution of a solid (sea water to drinking water). Fractional distillation: two miscible liquids (water and ethanol).
